what: Side-by-side cylinders (four by default — vase, pillar, tube) are drawn as 1px line art and the camera rotates with scroll — a vertical row of four black dots seen from above (0~16%: the fill drops out leaving hollow circles) → a tilted view (36%) → upright front view (56%) → turned 38° sideways (80%) → isometric view from 24° above (100%), with smoothstep between scenes. Each cylinder has its outer outline filled with the background color and is drawn farthest first so lines behind are hidden. A top rim ellipse and one inner glass tube line (transparent .55). With scene: room, a round-ended table, four legs, a bench and a wall corner are drawn over progress 0~70%, and from 45% three vases of different sizes (2·3·4 lines) grow starting from their outlines

options.path: story (default, dot → circle → lying down → front → turning → isometric) · front (one slightly angled front view — dimension drawing) · turn (turns from −40° to 40° from the front)
options.scene: When room, a scene of three vases on a table·bench (lines are drawn as progress advances)
options.scroll: With off, it isn’t tied to scroll — just a single first scene (or last scene)
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Slot that holds the drawing canvas — usually a slot pinned to the screen with position: sticky. If none, the element itself
options.size: Picture size — scale relative to the cell (width/(tube count×1.86+2.4), height/11), default 1. About .4 in a full-screen cell (original vase width ≈ 16% of screen)
options.--fx-tube-fill: Dot (fill) color seen from above, default --kf-ink

from.where: index.html .story__spin (dot → line vase rotation) · .story__room (three vases on a table) · detail.html dimension drawing — the original flips through pre-baked SVG line frames (vase-spin · turn · toiso) by scroll (scrub .4)

note: The original passes line-frame data extracted from a 3D model, which is not used — instead a cylinder is computed in orthographic projection every frame to redraw the same scene order. The wavy base line and dimension lines at the bottom of the original were not carried over
